graphEvents.label: Ask path accepts two transcript shapes
DSH decline start is an outcome not a representation loss

label: The ask path accepts exactly two transcript shapes: an offered COMMAND: line, or a final assistant text containing a question mark and a token naming the expected command; a prose ask without the mark classifies as none.

The ask classification fired once across five runtimes and two arms: each runtime carries five ask-policy rows per arm and workflow.asked reads claude 1 off and 0 on, opencode 0, pi 0, devin 0 and dsh 0, so the arm carries almost no ask-path evidence.

The dsh decline start is an outcome difference, not a representation loss: /deep:review was offered with policy ask, briefDelivered is true on both on-arm runs, changedPaths is empty on both, and the session text carries twelve COMMAND declined lines before /create:sk-skill was counted as the start.

The model own offer line is the only offer signal that moves with the brief: offerSeen off to on reads dsh 2 to 7, opencode 0 to 2, claude 0 to 0, pi 1 to 1, devin 3 to 3, and it survives opencode missing delivery reader.

Devin is the only runtime whose refusal path is observable, with offerDeclined 1 in both arms against 0 everywhere else; the single asked classification belongs to claude off, so asking and declining were each observed on a different runtime and never together.
